action.action-desc: Ms. Malliotakis (for herself, Mr. Schrader, Mr. Westerman, Mr. Young, and Mr. Bishop of Georgia) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Agriculture, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Labor, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To provide support for urban forests, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Urban Forests Act of 2021.

subsection.text: Section 9 of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105) is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating subsections (h) and (i) as subsections (j) and (k), respectively; and
by inserting after subsection (g) the following;
The Secretary shall establish a grant program to be known as the Tree City USA Grant Program to provide competitive grants to eligible entities to enhance and maintain urban forests.

subparagraph.text: To be eligible to be awarded a grant under paragraph (1), an eligible entity shall submit an application to the Secretary at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a proposal to enhance and maintain urban forests.
A non-profit organization that partners with an eligible entity may submit an application under subparagraph (A) on behalf of such eligible entity.

paragraph.text: In awarding grants under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall give priority to eligible entities that submit proposals under paragraph (2)(A) that—

subparagraph.text: enhance, maintain, or improve access to urban forests in—

clause.text: areas with low tree or environmental equity;

subparagraph.text: further a statewide assessment or local government initiative to enhance and maintain urban forests;
include a plan to mitigate risks from insects, disease, and non-native invasive species; and
include a plan to monitor and maintain new and existing trees.

paragraph.text: The Secretary may provide technical assistance to local governments to assist such local governments with—

subparagraph.text: becoming eligible entities; and
proposals under paragraph (2)(A).

paragraph.text: An eligible entity that receives a grant under this subsection shall contribute an amount of non-Federal funds (in cash or in kind) that is at least equal to the amount of the Federal funds received.

Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of the Urban Forests Act of 2021, and annually through 2030 thereafter, the Secretary shall designate as a Premier Tree City one eligible entity awarded a grant under this subsection to recognize the superior efforts of such eligible entity in enhancing and maintaining urban forests.
In addition to the amounts authorized under subsection (k), there are authorized to be appropriated $1,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2021 through 2030 to carry out this subsection.
In this subsection, the term eligible entity means a local government that—

subparagraph.text: serves an urban and community area; and
a tree planting non-profit organization recognizes as having—

clause.text: a community forestry program with an annual budget of at least $2 per capita; and
an Arbor Day observance and proclamation.

subsection.header: Cooperative agreements for urban wood utilization
subsection.text: Section 9 of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105), as amended by subsection (a), is further amended by inserting after subsection (h) the following:

subsection.header: Pilot project for cooperative agreements for urban wood utilization

paragraph.text: The Secretary may enter into cooperative agreements with State and local governments, institutions of higher education, private or non-profit organizations, and other entities that support projects that create wood products from dead and fallen trees in urban and community areas.
The Secretary shall prioritize entering into cooperative agreements that—

subparagraph.text: support local job creation;
are located in typically underserved areas or areas with low tree or environmental equity;
develop new uses for dead and fallen trees; and
improve urban forest health and resiliency.

paragraph.text: The Secretary may provide technical or financial assistance to entities that enter into a cooperative agreement under paragraph (1) to facilitate—

subparagraph.text: research on new uses for dead and fallen trees in urban and community areas; and
market expansion opportunities for products made from dead and fallen trees in urban and community areas.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of the Urban Forests Act of 2021, the Secretary shall provide a report to the relevant committees on—

subparagraph.text: the implementation of this subsection; and
recommendations to encourage economic development and job creation by creating new markets for wood products made from urban timber sources.

paragraph.text: In this subsection—

subparagraph.text: The term dead and fallen trees means trees that—

clause.text: have partially or completely fallen over; or
have been negatively impacted by insects, disease, or weather-related disturbances.

subparagraph.text: The term relevant committees means—

clause.text: the Committees on Natural Resources and Agriculture of the House of Representatives; and
the Committees on Energy and Natural Resources and Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate.

subsection.header: Program of education and technical assistance clarification for carbon storage
subsection.text: Section 9(d)(3) of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105(d)(3)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (C), by striking and after the semicolon;
in subparagraph (D), by inserting and after the semicolon; and
by inserting at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: identifying opportunities to increase carbon storage through afforestation and scientific urban and community forestry management;

subsection.header: National urban and community forestry advisory council
subsection.text: Section 9(g) of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105(g)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (2), by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: The Council established under this subsection shall meet not less than twice annually.

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

subparagraph.text: Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of the Urban Forests Act of 2021, the Secretary shall renew the Council.
The Council shall not terminate except as provided by an Act of Congress.

subsection.header: Urban and community forestry action plan clarification for carbon storage
subsection.text: Section 9(g)(3) of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105(g)(3)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.text: Recommendations for identifying opportunities to increase carbon storage through afforestation and scientific urban and community forestry management.

subsection.text: Subsection (k) of section 9 of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105), as redesignated by subsection (a), is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking $30,000,000 and inserting $50,000,000; and
by striking fiscal years 1991 through 1995 and inserting fiscal years 2021 through 2025.

section.header: Civilian Conservation Center urban forestry demonstration program
section.text: Section 147(d) of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (29 U.S.C. 3197(d)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this paragraph, the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Labor shall jointly establish Civilian Conservation Centers in urban and community areas (as defined in subsection (j) of section 9 of the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2105)).

In addition to the training and skills required under paragraph (1), the Civilian Conservation Centers established pursuant to subparagraph (A) shall provide training on urban forestry issues, including urban forest conservation, management, maintenance, and monitoring.

section.text: Section 3(e)(3) of the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 1642(e)(3)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (B), by striking and at the end;
in subparagraph (C)—

subparagraph.text: by inserting , including forest carbon before over the previous; and
by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by adding at the end the following:
demonstrates the efforts taken by the Forest Service to—

clause.text: conduct a strategic national forest inventory by measuring a statistically designed consistent historical series of field plots in combination with advanced technology to improve data, information, and estimates of precision; and
use advanced geospatial technologies to improve the area and volume estimates described in clause (i), especially for sub-State regions and smaller areas.

section.header: Memorandum of understanding to coordinate urban forestry programs
section.text: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture shall enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Secretaries of Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Interior, Labor, and Transportation and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to—

paragraph.text: identify strategies to increase equitable access to urban forests through existing programs and authorities;
coordinate existing urban forestry programs;
conduct research on the benefits of urban forests for air quality, heat island mitigation, energy burden reduction, and enhanced shading for heat-resilient housing and active transit; and
conduct research on improving coordination between the agencies to address insects, disease, and non-native invasive species in urban and community areas.
